title: Configuration rollback restarts OBS stream after setup failure
test: Scratch probe .arbitra/dev-notes/results/check-18-probe.mjs.txt (output in check-18-probe-output.txt): a fake OBS WebSocket with real state (the stream follows StartStream/StopStream, the service follows SetStreamServiceSettings) runs configureObsStream from the lane's src/lib/obsWebSocket.js (dev 4daa571) and from a copy of ac1c688's src/lib/obsWebSocket.js + obsOutputModel.mjs, in five cases: OBS idle and setup fails (no AV1 encoder); OBS live at its own target and setup fails (no AV1 encoder); OBS live and an auto-start the WHIP target refuses; OBS retrying an earlier target and setup fails; OBS live and the video settings refused. Plus the existing tests that pin the restart, 'OBS configuration rollback restores mutations in reverse order', 'a rollback starts the stream again only after the video settle time has passed since the last video restore' and 'a video color restore counts for the settle time, ...' (node --test tests/obsWebSocket.test.js tests/obsWebSocketWire.test.js: 52/52 pass).
proof: The mechanism the claim describes is right, the defect is not: the restart is the rollback restoring the stream OBS had before the setup, by design. configureObsStream does stop through the transaction (src/lib/obsWebSocket.js:812 stopActiveStream(sendRequest), sendRequest = transaction.request at :766; ac1c688 :579), the StopStream is journaled with a StartStream inverse (:514-519, :641, :668; ac1c688 :490-493) and a failed setup replays it (:678). But it is journaled first, so it is replayed last, after the previous stream service, video and profile values are restored: what restarts is the user's own earlier stream at its own target, not a broadcast to the Nextra room. The probe shows it on both versions: OBS live at rtmp://live.example/app, setup fails for want of an AV1 encoder -> 'StopStream (was active at rtmp://live.example/app) | GetStreamServiceSettings | SetStreamServiceSettings -> http://127.0.0.1:8889/whip/ROOM | SetStreamServiceSettings -> rtmp://live.example/app | StartStream at rtmp://live.example/app', result 'No AV1 OBS encoders were configured for this host. OBS settings were restored. ...', before and after 'stream active at rtmp://live.example/app'; with an auto-start the WHIP target refuses the end state is the same; with OBS idle no StartStream is replayed and OBS ends idle. That the restart is intended is in the code and the owner's own text: the transaction's doc (:528-540) and streamInverse ('Starting the stream undoes stopping it'), the test-stream comment that only Nextra's own start/stop pair is housekeeping that 'a failed setup' should not roll back (:838-841; ac1c688 :606-608), src/HostView.jsx:1555-1557, written in Release 2.1.0 before the audit (ac1c688 :1463-1465): 'a failed run can still leave OBS streaming (rollback restarts it)', with a control channel opened for exactly that stream, and audits-codex/REMAINING-WORK.md at a7d610b (:114-117) 'snapshots stream service, video, profile, output, and stream-state mutations, restores them in reverse order after a later failure'. This plan's TASK-079 built on it (a stop gate and the 1200 ms settle before 'a StartStream inverse'), and its tests above pin it. Sending the stop raw, as the claim implies, would make a failed setup end the user's live broadcast for good. The claim's examples are also partly wrong: a wrong OBS password fails at Identify, before the setup callback runs (:184, :212-214, the callback is called only on op 2 at :222-235), so nothing is stopped; a refused resolution is only a warning (:848-855) and commits (probe: success=true, 'Warnings: resolution (invalid resolution)'). Only setup failures (no usable encoder, encoder not verified, x264 for AV1, auto-start failed or stopped at once), an exception and the deadline roll back. Original code: same journaling and order at ac1c688, so not a defect there either; the only difference in the probe is the auto-start case, where ac1c688 added 'Rollback incomplete: StopStream: not active' (fixed by TASK-079, a different issue). No file changed.
